column11: Jynarque (tolvaptan), the only approved therapy for ADPKD and a daily oral: Otsuka's wholesale acquisition cost of $21,570.93 per 4-weekly blister kit (every strength, e.g. NDC 59148008928, 90mg/30mg), effective 2025-01-01 after a $1,411.18 increase (California HCAI, Prescription Drug WAC Increases, Q1-Q4 2025, data.chhs.ca.gov resource 46b78eef-5952-4fff-84c7-1fa758990ce8). One kit is 28 days (Otsuka launch release, 2018-04-24: 'sold in a 28-day treatment pack'), so 21,570.93 x 365/28 = $281,192 a year, the pack-to-year conversion the Kalydeco WAC takes in vrtx_prices.csv. No later Jynarque increase appears in the September 2026 monthly update of the same dataset
column12: a comparator, not a price this product has, and a published list price, which the book ranks above a CMS figure. Not in drug_demand because Otsuka is not in the universe. CMS Part D 2025 spend per beneficiary is $139,479.79 ($100,704,410.97 over 722 beneficiaries, 4,733 claims), about half the list, because 6.6 claims a beneficiary is a part year: generic tolvaptan entered in 2025 and took patients mid-year. The list was $13,041.10 per 28-day pack at the 2018 launch. Vertex prices its own genetic-disease orals higher still (Kalydeco WAC $378,786, vrtx_prices.csv)

column11: Rao V et al., Kidney360 2025;6(9):1522-1531 (doi:10.34067/KID.0000000816): 36 of 134 US adults on tolvaptan for ADPKD (27%) withdrew over a median follow-up of 28.2 months at two US centres. At a constant hazard 1 - 0.73^(12/28.2) = 12.53% of the stock stop each year, the rate the inaxaplin seed takes
column12: tolvaptan's stopping is driven by aquaretic side effects (10.4% of the cohort withdrew for them), which a PC1 corrector need not share, so this may run high

column11: JUDGEMENT: no Phase 3 is registered. AGLOW (NCT07161037), 26 patients, 52 weeks, completes 2027-07-22, so a registrational study starts in 2028 at the earliest. The analogue is inaxaplin, Vertex's other oral small molecule for a genetically defined kidney disease: AMPLITUDE (NCT05312879) started 2022-03-30 and the inaxaplin seed dates its first full year to 2028 from the interim readout Vertex has scheduled, about 5.75 years. A start in early 2028 plus 5.75 years gives a first full year of 2034
column12: an ADPKD label rests on kidney function outcomes that take years to accrue. Povetacicept went faster, its IgAN Phase 3 (NCT06564142) starting 2024-08-30 to a first full year of 2027 on an interim proteinuria readout and a priority review voucher, which no filing assigns to VX-407

column11: derived so the diagnosed pool holds at Willey's measured prevalence: with 20,186 diagnosed a year into 140,000, the untreated pool stays at 140,000 only if 140,000 / 160,186 = 0.874 of it remains eligible each year. The rest leave through kidney failure, death or the loss of eligibility a kidney-function floor imposes (AGLOW requires eGFR of at least 25)
column12: without it the engine carries every untreated patient forward at 1.0 and the eligible pool grows by the whole diagnosed inflow every year, which the stable measured prevalence rules out

column11: Three factors multiplied. (1) Variant subset, 0.10: the PKD1 variants VX-407 targets are 'up to approximately 10%' of people with ADPKD (Vertex FY2025 10-K, 0000875320-26-000056), 'up to approximately 30,000' (Q2 2026 release, 0000875320-26-000256). (2) Likely label, 315/523 = 0.602: AGLOW enrols Mayo imaging class 1B with htTKV of at least 250 mL/m and 1C to 1E, the high-risk classes, and in 523 ADPKD patients at Toronto's PKD centre 315 were class 1C to 1E (Calvaruso L et al., Sci Rep 2023;13:22257, doi:10.1038/s41598-023-48638-9). (3) Acceptance, 96/315 = 0.305: every high-risk patient at that centre was offered tolvaptan, the first disease-modifying ADPKD drug, and 96 of 315 were on it at last follow-up between 2016 and 2018; fewer than 2% of the 219 not on it had taken it before (Calvaruso 2023). 0.10 x 0.602 x 0.305 = 0.10 x 96/523 = 0.018356, about 2,570 US patients
column12: the acceptance share is tolvaptan's, and the commonest reason for refusing it was the aquaretic effect (51% of refusals), which a PC1 corrector need not share: case for higher. Case for lower: 10% is Vertex's upper bound, the centre is a specialist referral clinic that offered the drug to all, and VX-407 needs a genotype that most ADPKD patients have never had tested

derived: Vertex generated $12,074mm of free cash flow on $49,396mm of revenue over the five years to 2025, a 24.44% margin, against the 33.0% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Five years rather than three because operating cash flow was negative $493mm in 2024 on the Alpine acquisition, which takes a three-year window to 17.5% and lets one deal set the rate. Solved so the modelled book reproduces the margin rather than taken off a single line. Restated before interest: VRTX paid $195mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2021 to 2025, 0.39% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 10.33% to 9.94%. Restated at replacement capex: VRTX spent $1,375mm on plant over 2021 to 2025 against $758mm of plant depreciation, 1.25% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 9.94% to 8.47%. Restated without one-off cash: VRTX's free cash flow over 2021 to 2025 carried $6,517mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately. None recurs, so the charge falls from 8.47% to 0.00%. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 39.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2021 to 2025 supports 43.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.72%. It was held at nil, but VRTX books $20mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000875320-26-000056), 0.17% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -0.17%. Restated without working capital build: over 2021 to 2025 VRTX's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,164mm, inventories up $1,594mm, payables up $288mm, a working capital build of $2,470mm, 5.00% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -0.17% where the filed figures rebuild it at -4.72%, and stays there.
